title: Alvarez concludes that the real presence of things in eternity is the proper reason of God's certain knowledge
source_text: XXXI. In principio vero capitis sequentis inde colligit, Quod actualis existentia rerum in aeternitate, considerata ex parte divinae aeternitatis, est propria ratio, propter quam Deus certo cognoscit, omnia futura etiam contingentia. Idque quoniam ea quae sunt praesentia cognoscenti, quamvis secundum se contingentia sint, jam considerantur ut determinata, & ut determinate vera in ordine ad illam mensuram, in qua sunt praesentia, & in ordine ad cognitionem, qua ut praesentia sibi cognoscuntur.
pass_a_gloss: XXXI. But at the beginning of the following chapter he gathers thence, That the actual existence of things in eternity, considered on the part of divine eternity, is the proper reason, on account of which God certainly knows, all futures even contingent. And that because those things which are present to the knower, although according to themselves they be contingent, are now considered as determinate, and as determinately true in relation to that measure, in which they are present, and in relation to the knowledge, by which they are known as present to it.
pass_b_english: At the start of the next chapter he draws this conclusion: the actual existence of things in eternity, viewed from the side of God's eternity, is the proper reason why God knows all future things with certainty, contingent ones included.

The reason is that things present to a knower, though contingent in themselves, are already regarded as determinate. They are determinately true with respect to the measure in which they are present, and with respect to the knowledge by which they are known as present.

lemmas.gloss: the actual existence of things in eternity

choices.why: The Schools' term for future events without a necessary and determinate cause; kept as a technical term.
